headline_marked: ICT orders [[Sheikh Hasina and 29 others to surrender]] by Sept 16
headline: ICT orders Sheikh Hasina and 29 others to surrender by Sept 16
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has directed authorities to publish newspaper notices for the absconding accused in the 2013 Shapla Chattar crackdown case.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has ordered the publication of notices in two newspapers directing ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed, along with 27 others, to appear before the court on September 16.
The order comes after the prosecution reported that these 30 individuals could not be located at their registered addresses. Eleven other accused in the case are already in custody.
The case pertains to the crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka and in Narayanganj on May 5-6, 2013.

The tribunal previously issued arrest warrants for the accused, who are currently absconding. On July 27, the court accepted formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity against Sheikh Hasina and 40 others.
If the accused fail to appear or cannot be traced, the tribunal will appoint state-appointed lawyers to represent them and conduct the defense based on provided documents.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina, Gen Aziz, and Benazir Ahmed among 30 ordered to surrender by the ICT.

The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has ordered the publication of notices in two newspapers directing ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed, along with 27 others, to appear before the court on September 16.

The order comes after the prosecution reported that these 30 individuals could not be located at their registered addresses. Eleven other accused in the case are already in custody.

The case pertains to the crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka and in Narayanganj on May 5-6, 2013.

The tribunal previously issued arrest warrants for the accused, who are currently absconding. On July 27, the court accepted formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity against Sheikh Hasina and 40 others.

If the accused fail to appear or cannot be traced, the tribunal will appoint state-appointed lawyers to represent them and conduct the defense based on provided documents.

headline_marked: Floods in Nepal: [[Power supply to Bangladesh completely stopped]]
headline: Floods in Nepal: Power supply to Bangladesh completely stopped
summary: Severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi river area has shut down key hydropower projects, halting electricity exports to Bangladesh via India.
details: Electricity exports from Nepal to Bangladesh via India's transmission system have come to a complete standstill. This follows devastating floods in the Bhotekoshi river area that forced several hydropower projects to shut down.

The floods, which hit on August 26, have significantly reduced Nepal's overall electricity exports. While Nepal usually exports about 1,000 MW during the wet season, that figure has now dropped to approximately 650 MW.
Two specific projects approved for supply to Bangladesh were damaged: the 22.1 MW Chilime Hydropower Project and the 24 MW Trishuli Hydropower Project. Both have been offline since last week.

Nepal Electricity Authority's acting managing director, Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, stated that exports to Bangladesh have effectively dropped to zero. He noted that Nepal has requested India's permission to send power from alternative projects instead.
The disaster has been widespread, with a total of 12 hydropower projects in Nepal reporting production halts following the floods.
Separately, electricity supply from the Adani power plant in Godda, India, has also decreased. This is due to railway congestion and restrictions affecting coal transport to the plant.
